questions.question: A developer merges code suggested by GitHub Copilot, and the code later causes a production incident. According to responsible AI principles, who is accountable for the code?

options.text: The developer and the team that reviewed and merged the change
options.why: Correct. Accountability means people remain responsible for AI-assisted output they accept and ship.

options.text: GitHub, because Copilot generated the code
options.why: The tool provides suggestions. Responsibility for accepting and shipping code stays with people.

options.text: The model provider, because the model produced the suggestion
options.why: Model providers do not take responsibility for code that a team chooses to merge.

options.text: No one, because the code was generated automatically
options.why: Responsible AI requires that a person is always accountable for outcomes.

questions.explanation: The accountability principle states that people are responsible for AI systems and their results.

questions.question: A team adds a pull request template that asks contributors to state whether GitHub Copilot helped write the change. Which responsible AI principle does this practice support most directly?

options.text: Transparency
options.why: Correct. Disclosing AI involvement helps reviewers understand how the change was produced.

options.text: Inclusiveness
options.why: Inclusiveness concerns systems that work for people of all abilities and backgrounds.

options.text: Fairness
options.why: Fairness concerns avoiding biased treatment of groups of people.

options.text: Reliability and safety
options.why: Reliability and safety concern consistent, safe behavior. Disclosure is primarily a transparency practice.

questions.explanation: Transparency means people know when AI was involved and understand its limitations.

questions.question: GitHub Copilot generates a name validation regular expression that rejects names containing apostrophes or accented characters. Which responsible AI principles are MOST directly affected?

options.text: Fairness and inclusiveness
options.why: Correct. The validation treats some people unfairly and excludes users with names from many cultures.

options.text: Privacy and security
options.why: The issue does not expose data or weaken security.

options.text: Transparency and accountability
options.why: These principles concern disclosure and ownership, not biased behavior toward users.

options.text: Reliability and safety only
options.why: The code runs consistently. The core problem is that it excludes groups of people.

questions.explanation: Biased output that excludes groups of users conflicts with fairness and inclusiveness. Mitigate it with diverse test data and review.

questions.question: A company wants to reduce the risk of sensitive data being exposed when developers use GitHub Copilot Business. Which TWO actions should the company take?

options.text: Configure content exclusions for paths that contain sensitive configuration
options.why: Correct. Excluded files are not used as context and receive no inline suggestions in supported IDEs.

options.text: Instruct developers to use fictitious sample data instead of real customer records in prompts
options.why: Correct. Keeping personal data out of prompts reduces the risk of privacy leaks.

options.text: Set the public code filter to Allow
options.why: The public code filter addresses matches with public code, not exposure of sensitive data.

options.text: Ask developers to paste secrets into prompts only when Copilot needs them
options.why: Secrets should never be included in prompts.

questions.explanation: Content exclusions and the use of fake data are mitigations for privacy and security harms.

questions.question: You need to mitigate the risk that GitHub Copilot suggestions closely match code from public repositories with incompatible licenses. What should you configure?

options.text: The suggestions matching public code policy, set to Block or to Allow with code references reviewed
options.why: Correct. The policy either hides matching suggestions or shows code references with repository and license information.

options.text: Content exclusions for all public repositories
options.why: Content exclusions control which of your files Copilot uses as context. They do not filter matches with public code.

options.text: A custom instructions file that asks Copilot not to copy code
options.why: Instructions guide responses but do not provide a reliable filter for public code matches.

options.text: Copilot code review as a required reviewer
options.why: Copilot code review comments on pull requests. It is not a public code matching control.

questions.explanation: The public code filter is the mitigation for IP and licensing harms. Developers remain responsible for checking licenses.
